objective: Make the M0 JavaScript effect walk correct against NULL AST children, so discovery reads every file it is given instead of dying on one.
falsifiable_claim: The claim fails if any TypeScript source the estate may legitimately contain can make the effect walk throw rather than yield effects.
in_scope: Correct the null/undefined asymmetry through the effect walk: the loop guard at unwrapJavaScriptExpression tests `current !== undefined` and the caller at resolveJavaScriptEffect tests `expression === undefined`, so a NULL child passes every guard and dies in the first predicate that reads .kind.
Establish, with evidence, which files begin contributing census entries once the walk stops throwing -- because that is a change to what the census can SEE.
out_of_scope: Fixing this inside the M5 QM adoption cut. Null-tolerant guards change census semantics: files that previously crashed would start contributing entries, and a change to what a census can see gets its own cut and its own review.
Skip-and-continue. A file the walk cannot read can contain a route -- the file that exposed this defect is literally apps/ioi-ai/src/api/routes/admin/sessions.ts.

aggregate_disposition.why: Owner ruling 2026-08-04. Filed, not fixed inline. With the declared discovery exclusion in place the path is unreachable from estate sources, so filing is honest and sufficient; fixing it changes census semantics and must be reviewed as such.

implementation_actions: Audit every undefined-shaped guard on the effect-walk path and make it null-safe.
Re-run discovery over the adopted tree with the exclusion dropped and record the delta in census entries.
Only then consider dropping the apps/ioi-ai/ exclusion.
positive_proof: The effect walk completes over the adopted upstream tree with no throw and no skipped file.
The census-entry delta from making the walk null-safe is measured and recorded before the exclusion is dropped.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Reject a fix that makes the walk null-TOLERANT by skipping the node: skipping a subtree silently narrows what the census sees, which is the defect this record exists to remove, not a fix for it.
Reject dropping the apps/ioi-ai/ exclusion before the census-entry delta is measured -- discovery widening unobserved is how a blind spot becomes an unnoticed claim.
remaining_nonclaims: This record does not claim the adopted upstream tree is defective. THE ADOPTED TREE DID NOT BREAK M0 -- IT REVEALED M0. The null/undefined asymmetry is ours and was always there; estate sources simply never produced the AST shape that exposes it.
This record does not claim the frame chain is the only path to the defect; it is the one reproduced.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if null-safety cannot be achieved without narrowing what the walk reports; a walk that sees less is worse than one that refuses loudly.
current_implementation_evidence: FILED 2026-08-04 from the M5 QM adoption. Reproduced independently in a detached worktree at 83529c984 with node --stack-trace-limit=120 (node_modules symlinked; the scratch tree has none): 91 frames, entirely in scripts/lib/m0-program-control.mjs -- unwrapJavaScriptExpression:2571 reading .kind of null, reached via resolveJavaScriptEffect:2933, memberEffectDescriptor:2871 in mutual recursion with resolveJavaScriptEffect:2984, from visit:3242 under deep ts.forEachChild recursion. THE DEFECT IS SYSTEMIC, WHICH IS WHY THREE INDIVIDUAL PATCHES MISSED IT: there is no single throw site, because every guard in the chain is undefined-shaped and a null passes all of them. The exposing file is apps/ioi-ai/src/api/routes/admin/sessions.ts. Transcript and a repro head retained at docs/evidence/m0-effect-walk-null/.
